articles.title: AI Gateway Configuration Changes: Validate, Reload, Verify, and Roll Back
articles.excerpt: Originally published by Yilia Lin on API7.ai on 2026-11-09. This republication was prepared with AI assistance. The original article’s drafting process has not been verified. An AI gateway configurati…
articles.body: Originally published by Yilia Lin on API7.ai on 2026-11-09. This republication was prepared with AI assistance. The original article’s drafting process has not been verified. An AI gateway configuration change is complete only when four separate gates pass: the candidate file is valid, the gateway accepts it, the effective configuration changes as intended, and caller behavior still meets its contract. A healthy process alone is not proof that the new configuration was applied. This runbook uses AISIX OSS 1.8.0 in declarative file mode. It covers resources.yaml , offline validation, SIGHUP reload, /status/config , negative caller tests, and rollback to a known-good file.

articles.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
articles.excerpt: In October, we experienced eight incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services. The post GitHub availability report: October 2026 appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
articles.body: We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability. The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery. As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity.

articles.title: The Agentic Developer Stack in 2026: Memory, Skills, MCP, and Lock-In-Free Workflows
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. By 2026, the agentic developer stack has crystallized around three composable layers: persistent memory, declarative skills, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Bu…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . By 2026, the agentic developer stack has crystallized around three composable layers: persistent memory, declarative skills, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). But the tools that implement these layers — Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor — each ship their own opinionated config format. The result is a subtle lock-in trap: your workflow works beautifully inside one agent, but the moment you switch, your context, capabilities, and integrations vanish. This article dissects the anatomy of the modern agentic stack and shows you how to build a genuinely lock-in-free workflow that treats your agents as interchangeable runtimes over a shared, open substrate. 1. The Anatomy of an Agentic Developer Stack 2. Memory: The Persistent Context Layer 3.
articles.author: Tamiz Uddin

articles.title: I Open-Sourced a Tool That Proves What Your AI Agent Actually Did
articles.excerpt: AI agents are getting scary capable. Ask one to run a pentest, chain some automated operations, whatever — it's fast, it's thorough, and when it's done, it hands you a report. Why should you believe t…
articles.body: AI agents are getting scary capable. Ask one to run a pentest, chain some automated operations, whatever — it's fast, it's thorough, and when it's done, it hands you a report. Why should you believe that report? I treated that question as a threat-modeling problem, not a rhetorical one. Three failure paths, one by one: 1. Logs fail. The log runs in the same process and under the same privileges as the agent. Anything the agent can write, it can rewrite. A process that can edit its own log files produces evidence with zero forensic value for the question "what did this process do?" The basic requirement of evidence is independence from the party being examined. Same-process logging violates it completely. 2. Self-reports fail.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.excerpt: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.body: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P, then bounced twice and got lost. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P . To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement. The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired. When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space . The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down. Philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it . Images from Rosetta showed Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet.

articles.excerpt: For Katie Spicer, embracing opportunity and challenge has led to giant leaps during her time at NASA. Now as the NASA lander integration lead for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lander, one of the comm…
articles.body: 4 Min Read I Am Artemis Katie Spicer For Katie Spicer, embracing opportunity and challenge has led to giant leaps during her time at NASA. Now as the NASA lander integration lead for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lander, one of the commercially provided human landing systems for NASA’s Artemis program, Spicer will have her handprint on history. NASA’s Katie Spicer stands in front of the crew cabin prototype for Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 2 lunar lander. The lander is one of two commercial human landing systems that will help safely ferry astronauts from lunar orbit to the Moon’s surface and back for the agency’s crewed Artemis missions in 2028.
